  ```yaml
    method: codebase
    pattern: "ratchet.check"
    path: ".agents/scripts/complexity-scan-helper.sh"
  ```
- [ ] Outputs proposed thresholds when gap exceeds configured minimum (default 5)
- [ ] Returns exit 0 when ratchet-down is possible, exit 1 when thresholds are already tight
- [ ] Pulse integration creates a PR (or issue) when ratchet-down is available
- [ ] Proposed threshold is set to `actual_count + 2` (buffer for concurrent PRs)
- [ ] ShellCheck clean
  ```yaml

    method: bash
    run: "shellcheck .agents/scripts/complexity-scan-helper.sh"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- Buffer of +2 above actual count prevents flapping — concurrent PRs may temporarily increase violations before their simplification merges
- Gap threshold of 5 prevents noise — only propose ratcheting when meaningful reduction has accumulated
- The ratchet-check is idempotent — running it twice with no intervening changes produces the same proposal
- Bash 3.2 compat threshold (`BASH32_COMPAT_THRESHOLD`) is also ratchetable — include it in the check
- Comments documenting bump history in the config file are valuable audit trail — don't remove them, add a new ratchet-down comment

## Why

The triage comment is the thing that helps the maintainer decide whether to approve an issue. ## Why

On Linux systems with systemd, installing a systemd timer without removing the existing cron entry causes dual execution — the scheduled task fires twice. The uninstall only checks one backend, leaving orphan entries. This is a real bug affecting Linux deployments.

title: bug: dispatch_with_dedup Layer 7 false positive — claim/planning commits block unimplemented issues
body:
## Problem

The GH#17574 dedup layer (committed-to-main check) matches task IDs in **planning commits** on main and blocks dispatch, even though the task is not implemented.

## Evidence

Commit `8d5f37f1b` (`chore: claim t1910..t1915`) causes issues #17700, #17701, #17702, #17703, #17704 to be blocked with:
```
dispatch_with_dedup: Dispatch blocked for #17704 — task already committed to main (GH#17574)
```

Issue #440 is also blocked by the same check.

These issues are genuinely unimplemented — the matching commits are only claim/planning entries in TODO.md.

## Expected Behavior

The committed-to-main check should exclude commits with prefixes:
- `chore: claim`
- `plan:`
- `docs:`
- Commits that only modify `TODO.md`, `todo/`, or `AGENTS.md`

## Impact

**All dispatch is blocked** for the aidevops repo. The pulse cannot fill any worker slots because every open issue has a matching planning commit on main.

title: Proposal: HAND.toml — Declarative recurring operational processes for pulse
body:
## Summary

Proposal to add a **Hands** system to aidevops — declarative recurring autonomous jobs managed by the pulse supervisor. Hands fill the gap between one-shot task dispatch (GitHub issues) and manual launchd plists for recurring operational work.

## Problem

The pulse dispatches from a task queue (TODO.md / GitHub Issues). Every unit of work needs someone to create the task first. This works for development (features, bugs, refactors) but is clunky for recurring operational work:

- "Check competitor pricing every 6 hours"
- "Scan HN for mentions of our product daily"
- "Generate a weekly SEO performance report"
- "Monitor uptime and alert on Matrix if a site goes down"
- "Sweep stale PRs every morning"
- "Triage inbox every 15 minutes and draft responses"

Today you'd either create a launchd plist manually, or have the pulse create recurring GitHub Issues — both are awkward. There is no built-in mechanism for recurring agent-driven operational work.

## Proposed Design: Hands as Pulse-Managed Recurring Jobs

A Hand is a **declarative TOML definition of recurring autonomous work**. The pulse supervisor manages Hands alongside task dispatch — same process, same monitoring, same audit trail.

### File Structure

```
todo/hands/
  competitor-watch.toml
  seo-weekly-report.toml
  uptime-monitor.toml
  stale-pr-sweep.toml
  email-triage.toml
```

### HAND.toml Format

```toml
[hand]
name = "competitor-watch"
description = "Monitor competitor pricing pages for changes"
version = "1.0.0"

[schedule]
cron = "0 */6 * * *"           # Every 6 hours
timezone = "Europe/London"
jitter_minutes = 15            # Random delay to avoid thundering herd

[execution]
tier = "local"                 # local | haiku | sonnet | opus
fallback_tier = "haiku"
timeout_minutes = 30
max_retries = 2
retry_delay_minutes = 5

[execution.sandbox]
enabled = true
allow_network = ["api.github.com"]
allow_write = ["~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/hands/competitor-watch/"]

[context]
skills = ["competitor-intelligence", "web-design"]
repos = []
system_prompt = """
You are monitoring competitor pricing. Compare current prices against 
the baseline in data/competitor-baseline.json. Report only changes.
"""

[context.data]
dir = "~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/hands/competitor-watch/data"

[delivery]
channels = ["matrix:#ops-alerts"]
format = "markdown"
suppress_empty = true

[delivery.escalation]
confidence_threshold = 0.7
escalation_channel = "matrix:#justin-direct"

[budget]
max_cost_per_run = 0.50
max_cost_per_day = 2.00
max_cost_per_month = 30.00

[health]
alert_on_consecutive_failures = 3
alert_channel = "matrix:#ops-alerts"
expect_output_every = 3
```

### Pulse Integration (Phase 10)

The pulse supervisor gains a new phase:

```
Existing pulse cycle:
  Phase 1-8: Check capacity, scan GitHub, merge PRs, dispatch issues, sync TODOs...
  Phase 9: Memory audit

New:
  Phase 10: Hand scheduler
    1. Read all todo/hands/*.toml
    2. For each Hand, check if it's due (cron expression vs last_run timestamp)
    3. If due: dispatch via headless-runtime-helper.sh with the Hand's config
    4. Record run result in ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/hands/<name>/runs.jsonl
    5. Handle delivery (post to channels, escalate if needed)
    6. Handle health (alert on consecutive failures)
```

### State Tracking

Each Hand gets a run log:

```jsonl
{"run_id":"h-001","hand":"competitor-watch","started":"2026-04-02T12:00:00Z","completed":"2026-04-02T12:04:23Z","status":"success","findings":3,"cost":0.00,"model":"ollama/gemma4-agent","delivered_to":["matrix:#ops-alerts"]}
{"run_id":"h-002","hand":"competitor-watch","started":"2026-04-02T18:00:00Z","completed":"2026-04-02T18:03:11Z","status":"success","findings":0,"cost":0.00,"model":"ollama/gemma4-agent","delivered_to":null,"suppressed":true}
```

### CLI Interface

```bash
aidevops hands list                          # List all Hands and status
aidevops hands run competitor-watch          # Run immediately (bypass schedule)
aidevops hands pause competitor-watch        # Pause a Hand
aidevops hands resume competitor-watch       # Resume a Hand
aidevops hands history competitor-watch      # View run history
aidevops hands create --name "seo-weekly" --schedule "0 9 * * 1" --tier local
aidevops hands validate todo/hands/competitor-watch.toml
```

### Helper Script

`hands-helper.sh` with subcommands: `list`, `run`, `pause`, `resume`, `history`, `create`, `validate`, `health`, `cost-report`.

## Key Design Decisions

1. **Hands live in `todo/hands/`** — committed to git, version-controlled. The Hand definition is the documentation.
2. **Pulse manages the schedule, not launchd.** One scheduler manages both task dispatch and Hand execution. No proliferation of launchd plists.
3. **Hands use the same dispatch chain as tasks.** `headless-runtime-helper.sh run` with `--model`, `--prompt`, `--dir`. All backoff, rotation, and metrics infrastructure works unchanged.
4. **Persistent data directories.** Each Hand stores state across runs (baselines, dedup databases, historical data) in `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/hands/<name>/data/`.
5. **Delivery is first-class.** Tasks produce PRs. Hands produce reports/alerts delivered to configured channels.
6. **Budget controls are per-Hand.** Prevents runaway costs. Zero-cost when using local models (Ollama/Gemma 4).

## Hands vs Pulse — Comparison

| | Pulse (existing) | Hands (proposed) |
|---|---|---|
| Work source | External queue (TODO.md, GitHub Issues) | Self-contained TOML definition |
| Granularity | One-shot tasks with completion criteria | Recurring loops, no "done" state |
| Output | PRs, issue comments, code changes | Reports, alerts, data, messages |
| State | Task is open → in progress → closed | Always running (active/paused) |
| Best for | Development work, bug fixes, features | Monitoring, research, email, content ops |

## Context

This proposal emerged from designing a local model automation server (Mac Mini M4 Pro + Gemma 4 26B via Ollama). The Hands concept is inspired by OpenFang's autonomous "Hands" but adapted to work within aidevops's existing architecture — using the pulse as the scheduler and `headless-runtime-helper.sh` as the dispatch mechanism.

With local models running at zero marginal cost, recurring operational tasks become economically viable to automate with LLM reasoning rather than brittle scripts.

## Implementation Estimate

- `hands-helper.sh` with core subcommands: 2-3 days
- Pulse Phase 10 integration: 1-2 days
- TOML parser (Python or shell): 1 day
- Delivery routing (Matrix/email): 1-2 days (builds on existing `matrix-dispatch-helper.sh`)
- Total: ~1 week

@marcusquinn — would appreciate your thoughts on whether this fits the aidevops roadmap and any design concerns before implementation.

body:
**Task ID:** `t1918` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~1h (ai:30m test:15m read:10m)`
**Logged:** 2026-04-07
**Tags:** `bug` `security` `auto-dispatch`

## Description

fix: silent gh auth failure in approval-helper.sh under sudo on Linux — `_approve_target()` swallows `gh` auth errors via `>/dev/null 2>&1`, prints false `[OK]` when no approval comment is posted. Add `_require_gh_auth()` pre-check with `GH_TOKEN` workaround message, check `gh comment` exit codes, document `[owner/repo]` positional arg in AGENTS.md. Linux-only (gnome-keyring inaccessible under sudo), macOS unaffected.

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh:266-308` — add `_require_gh_auth()` function and check `gh` command exit codes in `_approve_target()`
- `EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md:168` — document `[owner/repo]` positional argument for `sudo aidevops approve`

### Implementation Steps

1. Add `_require_gh_auth()` function (model on existing `_require_approval_key()` at line 50):

```bash
_require_gh_auth() {
    if ! gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        _print_error "gh authentication failed (common under sudo on Linux — gnome-keyring is inaccessible)"
        _print_info "Workaround: export GH_TOKEN before sudo, or run: sudo GH_TOKEN=\$(gh auth token) aidevops approve ..."
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}
```

2. Call `_require_gh_auth` in `_approve_target()` after `_require_approval_key` (line 278):

```bash
    _require_approval_key "$actual_key" || return 1
    _require_gh_auth || return 1
```

3. Check exit code of `gh issue comment` / `gh pr comment` (lines 299-303) — don't print `[OK]` on failure:

```bash
    if [[ "$target_type" == "issue" ]]; then
        if ! gh issue comment "$target_number" --repo "$slug" --body "$comment_body"; then
            _print_error "Failed to post approval comment on issue #$target_number"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        if ! gh pr comment "$target_number" --repo "$slug" --body "$comment_body"; then
            _print_error "Failed to post approval comment on PR #$target_number"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
```

4. Update AGENTS.md to document the positional arg:

```markdown
`sudo aidevops approve issue <number> [owner/repo]`
```

# t1918: Fix silent gh auth failure in approval-helper.sh under sudo on Linux

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-04-07
- **Session:** claude-code:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (from review of GH#17754)
- **Conversation context:** User filed GH#17754 reporting that `sudo aidevops approve issue` silently fails on Linux when gnome-keyring is inaccessible under sudo. Review confirmed two bugs: silent `gh` auth failure and unchecked exit code.

## What

Fix `approval-helper.sh` so that `sudo aidevops approve` fails loudly when `gh` cannot authenticate, instead of printing a false `[OK]` message. Also document the `[owner/repo]` positional argument syntax in AGENTS.md.

## Why

The approval gate is a critical human-only security control (SSH-signed comments that workers cannot forge). A false success means the maintainer believes an issue is approved when no approval comment was posted — the issue stays unapproved but appears approved to the user. On Linux with gnome-keyring, `sudo` cannot access the desktop keyring session, so `gh` silently fails. macOS is unaffected (Keychain works under sudo with a password prompt).

## Tier

`tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Multi-point fix in one file requiring understanding of the sudo/keyring interaction. Narrative brief with file references is sufficient — no novel design needed.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh:266-308` — add `_require_gh_auth()` function and check `gh` command exit codes in `_approve_target()`
- `EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md:168` — document `[owner/repo]` positional argument for `sudo aidevops approve`

### Implementation Steps

1. Add `_require_gh_auth()` function (model on existing `_require_approval_key()` at line 50):

```bash
_require_gh_auth() {
    if ! gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        _print_error "gh authentication failed (common under sudo on Linux — gnome-keyring is inaccessible)"
        _print_info "Workaround: export GH_TOKEN before sudo, or run: sudo GH_TOKEN=\$(gh auth token) aidevops approve ..."
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}
```

2. Call `_require_gh_auth` in `_approve_target()` after `_require_approval_key` (line 278):

```bash
    _require_approval_key "$actual_key" || return 1
    _require_gh_auth || return 1
```

3. Check exit code of `gh issue comment` / `gh pr comment` (lines 299-303) — don't print `[OK]` on failure:

```bash
    if [[ "$target_type" == "issue" ]]; then
        if ! gh issue comment "$target_number" --repo "$slug" --body "$comment_body"; then
            _print_error "Failed to post approval comment on issue #$target_number"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        if ! gh pr comment "$target_number" --repo "$slug" --body "$comment_body"; then
            _print_error "Failed to post approval comment on PR #$target_number"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
```

4. Update AGENTS.md to document the positional arg:

```markdown
`sudo aidevops approve issue <number> [owner/repo]`
```

### Verification

```bash
# ShellCheck passes
shellcheck .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh

# Function exists
grep -q '_require_gh_auth' .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh

# Exit code is checked (no more silent >/dev/null 2>&1 on gh comment calls)
! grep -q 'gh issue comment.*>/dev/null 2>&1' .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh
! grep -q 'gh pr comment.*>/dev/null 2>&1' .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh

# AGENTS.md documents the positional arg
grep -q 'owner/repo' .agents/AGENTS.md | grep -q 'approve'
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_require_gh_auth()` function exists and is called before posting approval comments
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "_require_gh_auth"
    path: ".agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh"
  ```
- [ ] `gh issue comment` and `gh pr comment` exit codes are checked — failure prevents false `[OK]`
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "! grep -q 'gh issue comment.*>/dev/null 2>&1' .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh && ! grep -q 'gh pr comment.*>/dev/null 2>&1' .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh"
  ```
- [ ] Error message includes actionable workaround (`GH_TOKEN` export)
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "GH_TOKEN"
    path: ".agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh"
  ```
- [ ] AGENTS.md documents `[owner/repo]` positional argument syntax
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "grep 'approve' .agents/AGENTS.md | grep -q 'owner/repo'"
  ```
- [ ] ShellCheck clean
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "shellcheck .agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- **Why option 1 (detect + error) over option 2 (auto-resolve token):** Auto-resolving the token before sudo escalation requires restructuring the sudo boundary. The helper is designed to be invoked after sudo, so the token would need to be passed as an env var from a wrapper. Clear error message with workaround is sufficient and lower complexity.
- **macOS unaffected:** Keychain works under sudo (with password prompt). This is Linux-specific but the fix is cross-platform safe.
- **Root cause is gnome-keyring isolation:** `sudo` creates a new session without `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, so `gh` cannot reach the credential store. `GH_TOKEN` env var bypasses the credential store entirely.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh:266-308` — `_approve_target()` function with the bugs
- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh:50-60` — `_require_approval_key()` pattern to follow
- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh:580` — help text (already documents positional arg syntax)
- `.agents/AGENTS.md:168` — approval docs (missing `[owner/repo]` syntax)

- **Blocked by:** none

# Task Brief - t1919: Fix resolve_api_key subshell export bug

## Context
- **Session Origin**: Interactive review of GH#17755
- **Issue**: [GH#17755](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/17755)
- **File**: `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh`

## What
Fix `resolve_api_key()` so API key resolution works when called via `$()` command substitution. Currently, `export` inside the subshell never reaches the parent shell, causing headless worker dispatch to fail in clean environments.

## Why
`probe_provider()` calls `resolve_api_key` in a `$()` subshell (L796). The `export` at L314 (gopass) and `source` at L327 (credentials.sh) only affect the subshell's environment. When `_get_key_value()` (L340) subsequently checks `${!var_name}` in the parent shell, the variable is empty — returning exit 3 ("Key var found but empty"). This blocks all headless dispatch when keys aren't pre-loaded in the environment.

## How
1. EDIT: `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh:285-337` — change `resolve_api_key()` to echo the resolved key value directly instead of relying on `export` side-effects. Update the security comment at L283 to document that the function now outputs the key value (callers must capture in local vars, never log).
2. EDIT: `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh:794-806` — simplify `probe_provider()` to use a single call: `api_key=$(resolve_api_key "$provider")`. Remove the separate `_get_key_value` call.
3. EDIT: `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh:340-361` — review `_get_key_value()` for removal or update to match new semantics.
4. EDIT: `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh:1359-1364` — update `cmd_probe()` call site to match new `resolve_api_key` return semantics.

**Reference pattern**: Follow standard shell idiom — functions echo values, callers capture via `$()`. Model on existing helper functions that already use this pattern.

**Security consideration**: `resolve_api_key` currently echoes the var name (not the value) with a security comment at L283. The fix changes this — callers must ensure the value is captured in a `local` variable and never logged/printed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `resolve_api_key` echoes the key value directly (not the var name).
- [ ] `probe_provider` works in a clean subshell environment (no pre-loaded keys).
- [ ] `_get_key_value` is updated or removed.

title: bug: issue-sync.yml sync-on-pr-merge crashes on locked issues (missing error handling)
body:
## Description

The `sync-on-pr-merge` job in `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` crashes when the linked issue is locked. The `gh issue comment` call on line 388 has no error handling, so a locked issue causes the entire job to abort — including the downstream TODO.md proof-log and PLANS.md sync steps.

This is inconsistent with the same file's conventions: the label operations on lines 395–400 all use `2>/dev/null || true`, and the `gh pr comment` on line 739 uses `2>/dev/null || echo "::warning::..."`. Only the closing comment on line 388 is unguarded.

## Expected Behavior

When a PR merges and the linked issue is locked, the closing comment should be skipped gracefully (with a warning), and the remaining steps (labels, TODO.md proof-log, PLANS.md sync) should still execute.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a repo using the canonical `issue-sync.yml` from aidevops
2. Lock a completed issue (e.g., lock as "resolved")
3. Merge a PR whose title references a task linked to that locked issue
4. The `sync-on-pr-merge` job fails at the `gh issue comment` step with:
   `GraphQL: Unable to create comment because issue is locked (addComment)`
5. TODO.md proof-log and PLANS.md sync steps are skipped

## Observed Impact

## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/tools/context/pageindex.md`
**Detected topic:** PageIndex - Vectorless Reasoning-Based RAG
**Current size:** 153 lines

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after

### Confidence: medium

Automated scan flagged this file for maintainer review. The best simplification strategy requires human judgment — some files are appropriately structured already. Reference corpora (SKILL.md, domain knowledge bases) need restructuring into chapters, not content reduction.

title: t1922: derive headless model list from pool + routing table — remove AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_MODELS env var
body:
## What

Remove `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_MODELS` and `PULSE_MODEL` as user-configurable env vars. The framework derives the headless model list automatically from two existing sources:

1. **Pool** (`oauth-pool-helper.sh list all`) — which providers the user has accounts for (anthropic, openai, etc.)
2. **Routing table** (`configs/model-routing-table.json`) — which models map to which tiers per provider

The round-robin model list = "for each provider in the pool, get the sonnet-tier model from the routing table." No user configuration needed.

## Why

`AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_MODELS` was set in `credentials.sh` (a user-owned file that survives updates). When the framework updated model mappings (gpt-5.3-codex → gpt-5.4), the stale env var persisted and caused ~50% of worker dispatches to fail silently for hours. This class of bug is eliminated entirely by deriving the list at runtime.

Secondary: `credentials.sh` should only contain secrets. Mixing operational config with API keys creates confusion and prevents the framework from managing its own settings.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:312-362` — `get_configured_models()` 
  - Instead of reading `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_MODELS`, query the pool for available providers, then look up each provider's sonnet-tier model in the routing table
  - Keep a hardcoded `DEFAULT_HEADLESS_MODELS` as absolute fallback if both pool and routing table are unavailable
  - Remove the `_is_non_agentic_model` / `_get_agentic_replacement` functions (no longer needed — the routing table is the source of truth, codex models will never appear)

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — anywhere `PULSE_MODEL` is referenced
  - The pulse should use the routing table's sonnet tier directly, not an env var

- **EDIT**: `.agents/automate.md:114-119` — remove the `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_MODELS` export from setup docs. Replace with explanation that the framework auto-detects from the pool.

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/commands/pulse.md` — update any references to model env vars

- **EDIT**: `.agents/tools/context/model-routing.md` — document the new derivation flow

### Critical constraints

1. **Never confuse aidevops OAuth pool with OpenCode's OAuth** — different auth flows, different stores, different rotation logic. The pool helper (`oauth-pool-helper.sh`) is our system. OpenCode's `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` is theirs. Only query our pool.

2. **Pool query must be cheap** — `oauth-pool-helper.sh list all` reads a JSON file, no API calls. Safe to call every dispatch cycle.

3. **Backward compatibility** — if `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_MODELS` is still set (user hasn't cleaned up credentials.sh), log a deprecation warning but respect it as an override for one release cycle. Remove the override path in the following release.

4. **The pool is the authority on accounts, the routing table is the authority on models** — don't mix these concerns. The derivation logic is: pool → providers → routing table → models.

### Verification

```bash
# After change: this should work without AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_MODELS set
unset AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_MODELS
bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh select --role worker
# Should return a valid model from the routing table based on pool providers

# Verify no codex models appear
bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh select --role worker | grep -v codex
```

## Acceptance criteria

1. Workers dispatch with correct models without any env var overrides
2. Pool with only Anthropic accounts → only Anthropic models in round-robin
3. Pool with Anthropic + OpenAI → both providers' sonnet models in round-robin
4. No codex/code-completion models ever appear in the model list
5. Deprecation warning logged if legacy env var is still set
6. `automate.md` updated to remove the export instructions

## Additional: setup/update cleanup

`setup.sh` and `aidevops update` should actively clean up stale config from `credentials.sh`:

- **Remove** `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_MODELS` export lines (no longer user-configurable)
- **Remove** `PULSE_MODEL` export lines (framework-managed)
- **Remove** `AIDEVOPS_ACTIVE_TENANT` if it duplicates the default
- **Leave** all actual secrets (API keys, tokens) untouched

Implementation: a `_cleanup_legacy_config()` function in `setup.sh` that runs on every `aidevops update`. Uses `sed` to comment out (not delete) deprecated lines with a note: `# DEPRECATED by aidevops v3.7+ — model routing is now automatic`. This preserves the user's file history while preventing stale values from being sourced.

Also clean up `tenants/*/credentials.sh` with the same logic.

### Verification
```bash
# After update, these should not be exported
env | grep -E 'AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_MODELS|PULSE_MODEL' | wc -l
# Should return 0
```

title: bug: _is_task_committed_to_main false positive — git --grep matches task ID cross-references in commit bodies
body:
## Description

`_is_task_committed_to_main()` in `pulse-wrapper.sh` uses `git log --grep="$pattern"` for Pattern 1 (`tNNN` task IDs). `--grep` searches the **entire commit message** (subject + body), not just the subject. When a code commit cross-references other task IDs in its body text (e.g., documenting what a schema field is for), those tasks are falsely classified as "already committed to main" and permanently blocked from dispatch.

This is a distinct variant from #17707 (planning commit subjects) and #17761 (`p00N:` prefix / `docs/` paths). Both previous fixes are deployed and working — this gap is specifically about **body cross-references in non-planning code commits** that pass both the subject-line filter and the path-based filter.

## Reproduction

Affected function: `pulse-wrapper.sh:6711-6815` (`_is_task_committed_to_main`)

**Scenario:** A commit implements task `t112` and its subject is `feat: t112 storage refinement — auto-archive to S3 (#867)`. In the commit body, it documents related tasks:

```
- scope_match: required flag; feeds scope-aware extraction (t100/t101)
- known_communities: list[str] — seed forums for community discovery (t107)
- domain_caps: fnmatch patterns; replaces global limit (t104)
```

These are documentation cross-references — the commit does not implement t101, t104, or t107.

**Step-by-step trace (reproducible on any repo with this pattern):**

```bash
# 1. Pattern 1 extracts bare "t101" from issue title "t101: Scope-aware extraction"

# 2. git log --grep="t101" matches the body cross-reference:
git log origin/main --since="$ISSUE_CREATED" -E --grep="t101" --format='%H %s'
# → abc1234 feat: t112 storage refinement ...   (WRONG — this is t112's commit, not t101's)

# 3. Subject-line filter passes it (starts with "feat:", not "chore: claim|plan:|p[0-9]+:"):
#    → passes through

# 4. Path-based filter passes it (touches real code files, not just planning files):
#    → src/module/schema.py, templates/*.yaml, tests/*.py — all code, not planning

# 5. Result: match_count=1, function returns 0 → dispatch permanently blocked for t101
```

**Observed impact** on a managed private repo:
- 3 issues with `status:available` + `auto-dispatch` are **permanently blocked** from dispatch — the pulse logs show `Dispatch blocked ... task already committed to main (GH#17574)` every cycle
- 1 additional issue would be blocked when its dependency status clears
- All false positives trace to exactly 2 commits that cross-reference other task IDs in their body text
- Verified across 5 task IDs with body-only matches; every one that survives both filter stages is a false positive

## Root Cause

`git log --grep` has no native "subject-only" mode — it always searches subject + body. Pattern 1 (`search_patterns+=("$task_id_match")`) adds a bare `tNNN` string with no structural anchoring, so any incidental mention in a commit body is a match.

The existing two-stage filter (subject-line prefix filter + path-based planning detection) cannot catch this because:
1. The commit has a legitimate non-planning subject (`feat:`, not `chore: claim` / `plan:` / `p00N:`)
2. The commit touches real code files (not just `TODO.md` / `todo/*` / `docs/*`)

The commit is correctly classified as "real code work" — but it's code work for a *different* task that happens to *mention* the target task ID.

## Proposed Fix

**For Patterns 1 (`tNNN`) and 2 (`GH#NNN`)**: replace `--grep` with subject-only matching via `--format` + `grep -w`.

Task ID conventions (`tNNN:`, `feat: tNNN`, `tNNN/tNNN:`) place the task ID in the **subject line**. Body mentions are always cross-references.

```bash
# Current (matches subject + body):
git -C "$repo_path" log origin/main --since="$created_at" \
    -E --grep="$pattern" --format='%H %s' |
    grep -vE '^[0-9a-f]+ (chore: claim|plan:|p[0-9]+:)' |
    cut -d' ' -f1

# Fixed (subject-only for Pattern 1/2):
git -C "$repo_path" log origin/main --since="$created_at" \
    --format='%H %s' |
    grep -wE "$pattern" |
    grep -vE '^[0-9a-f]+ (chore: claim|plan:|p[0-9]+:)' |
    cut -d' ' -f1
```

**Key details:**
- `grep -w` enforces word boundaries — prevents `t101` from matching `t1010` (substring collision, relevant for repos with 4+ digit task IDs like aidevops itself)
- Patterns 3-5 (`(#NNN)`, `Closes #NNN`, `Fixes #NNN`) should **keep using `--grep`** because closing keywords legitimately appear in commit bodies, and their syntactic structure prevents accidental matches
- This requires splitting the `for pattern in "${search_patterns[@]}"` loop into two paths based on pattern type, or tagging patterns with their match mode

**Implementation approach:** Tag patterns at creation time:

```bash
# At pattern creation (line ~6724-6748):
local -a subject_patterns=()  # Patterns 1, 2: subject-only
local -a message_patterns=()  # Patterns 3, 4, 5: full message

# Pattern 1
[[ -n "$task_id_match" ]] && subject_patterns+=("$task_id_match")
# Pattern 2
[[ -n "$gh_id_match" ]] && subject_patterns+=("$gh_id_match")
# Patterns 3-5
message_patterns+=("\\(#${issue_number}\\)")
message_patterns+=("[Cc]loses #${issue_number}")
message_patterns+=("[Ff]ixes #${issue_number}")
```

Then search each array with its appropriate method.

**Performance**: 274 commits over 6 days in the affected repo. Subject-only matching via `--format | grep` adds negligible overhead vs `--grep` — the commit set is already bounded by `--since`.

## Permutation Audit

Systematically checked all permutations of false positive in `_is_task_committed_to_main`:

| # | Permutation | Caught? | By which filter | Notes |
|---|-------------|---------|-----------------|-------|
| 1 | `chore: claim tNNN` | Yes | Subject filter | |
| 2 | `plan: ...` | Yes | Subject filter | |
| 3 | `p00N: ...` | Yes | Subject filter (#17761) | |
| 4 | Commit touches only `TODO.md`/`todo/*` | Yes | Path filter | |
| 5 | Commit touches only `docs/*` | Yes | Path filter (#17761) | |
| 6 | **Body cross-ref in code commit** | **No** | — | **This bug** |
| 7 | **Substring collision** (`t101` → `t1010`) | **No** | — | Fix: `grep -w` |
| 8 | `chore: mark tNNN complete` + non-planning files | Theoretical | Path filter saves today | All `chore: mark` commits audited (100+) touch only `TODO.md` |

The proposed fix addresses gaps 6 and 7. Gap 8 is theoretical only.

## Related Issues

- #17574 — Original: pulse dispatches for tasks already committed to main (introduced `_is_task_committed_to_main`)
- #17707 — Layer 1: planning subject prefixes (`chore: claim`, `plan:`) and path-based filter
- #17761 — Layer 2: `p00N:` prefix and `docs/*` paths

This is Layer 3: body cross-references in non-planning code commits.

## Environment

- aidevops: 3.6.159
- AI Assistant: OpenCode v1.3.17
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21
- gh CLI: 2.89.0

title: simplification: tighten agent doc Routines Reference (.agents/reference/routines.md, 62 lines)
body:
## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/reference/routines.md`
**Detected topic:** Routines Reference
**Current size:** 62 lines

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)
- Qlty smells resolved for the target file: `~/.qlty/bin/qlty smells --all 2>&1 | grep '.agents/reference/routines.md' | grep -c . | grep -q '^0$'` (report `SKIP` if Qlty is unavailable, not `FAIL`)
- For reference corpora: `wc -l` total of chapter files >= original line count minus index overhead

### Confidence: medium

Automated scan flagged this file for maintainer review. The best simplification strategy requires human judgment — some files are appropriately structured already. Reference corpora (SKILL.md, domain knowledge bases) need restructuring into chapters, not content reduction.

title: t2028: cch-extract.sh rejects Bun-compiled Claude CLI — the default install method
body:
## Summary

`cch-extract.sh` hard-rejects Bun-compiled Claude CLI binaries (ELF/Mach-O) at line 67-71, printing:

```
[ERROR] Bun binary detected. This script supports Node.js Claude CLI only.
```

This means `cch-constants.json` is never created, causing `provider-auth.mjs` to print `[aidevops] CCH: no cache found. Extracting constants...` on every OpenCode session start.

## Why this is wrong

The Bun-compiled binary **is** the default ("native") install method since Claude Code ~1.0. The npm/Node.js install is a legacy alternative. Anthropic's own code calls the Bun binary `"native"` and npm `"npm-global"`.

**Current install methods** (Claude Code 2.1.94):
| Method | Runtime | Format | Anthropic name |
|--------|---------|--------|----------------|
| `claude install` / `claude update` | Bun (compiled) | Single ELF/Mach-O binary ~220MB | `"native"` |
| `npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` | Node.js | `node_modules/` + `cli.js` | `"npm-global"` |
| homebrew, winget, pacman, etc. | Bun (compiled) | Package-managed binary | `"package-manager"` |

## The fix is straightforward

The constants (salt, version, char_indices) **are extractable** from the Bun binary via `strings`:

```bash
# VERSION — works
strings /path/to/claude | grep -oP 'VERSION:"\d+\.\d+\.\d+"'
# → VERSION:"2.1.94"

# char_indices — works
strings /path/to/claude | grep -oP '\[\d+,\d+,\d+\]\.map\('
# → [4,7,20].map(

# salt — works (filter known non-salt hex strings)
strings /path/to/claude | grep -oP '"[0-9a-f]{12}"' | grep -v '000000000000\|444444444444\|333333333333'
# → "59cf53e54c78"
```

## Worker Guidance

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/cch-extract.sh:60-78` — `find_claude_source()` function
- Instead of rejecting ELF/Mach-O binaries, pipe them through `strings` and write to a temp file, then let the existing Python regex extractors run on that temp file
- Alternative: run the Python extractors directly on `strings` output (pipe)
- The existing `extract_version()`, `extract_salt()`, `extract_char_indices()` regexes already work on the strings output — tested
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/cch-extract.sh:184-199` — `detect_cch_placeholder()` also needs the strings-extracted content
- Verification: `cch-extract.sh --cache && cat ~/.aidevops/cch-constants.json` should produce valid JSON with version, salt, char_indices

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cch-extract.sh` works with Bun-compiled Claude CLI (the default)
- [ ] `cch-extract.sh` still works with Node.js npm install (if present)
- [ ] `cch-extract.sh --cache` creates valid `~/.aidevops/cch-constants.json`
- [ ] ShellCheck clean
- [ ] `[aidevops] CCH: no cache found` message no longer appears on session start


---

title: fix(opencode-plugin): strip trailing assistant messages to prevent Claude 4.x prefill error
body:
## Problem

opencode webui (especially on mobile) intermittently returns:

> This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.

This rejects requests on Claude Opus/Sonnet 4.x (Anthropic native, GitHub Copilot, OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vertex — all providers that proxy these models).

## Root cause

Anthropic rejects conversations that end with an assistant message for Claude 4.x. This state occurs in opencode in three documented ways:

1. **Aborted/interrupted previous turn** ([sst/opencode#13768](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/13768), [PR #14772](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/14772)) — the aborted assistant has `finish` undefined, so the continuation gate at `session/prompt.ts` (`lastAssistant2?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(...)`) fails open and the next iteration calls the LLM with a trailing assistant still present. Common on mobile where flaky connections cause aborts.
2. **Continuation loop bug** ([sst/opencode#17982](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/17982), [PR #16921](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/16921)) — opencode 1.3.17 has a partial gate but it requires `finish` to be set.
3. **Max-steps hint** ([PR #14772](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/14772)) — when max steps is reached, opencode appends `{role: "assistant", content: max_steps_default}` after the plugin hook runs.

Three upstream PRs ([#14772](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/14772), [#16921](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/16921), [#18091](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/18091)) all add `stripTrailingAssistant()` in `provider/transform.ts`. **None are merged** as of opencode v1.3.17 / v1.4.0.

## Fix

Apply the same defensive strip at the plugin layer via `experimental.chat.messages.transform`, which runs immediately before `MessageV2.toModelMessages()` in `session/prompt.ts:837128`.

### Files

- `NEW: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/prefill-guard.mjs` — pure module exporting `createPrefillGuardHook(deps)`. Strips trailing assistant messages from `output.messages` only when safe (preserves messages with `finish === "tool-calls"` or active `pending`/`running`/`completed` tool parts so legitimate tool-call flows are untouched). Wrapped in try/catch so a bug here can never break the hook chain.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` — imports `createPrefillGuardHook`, composes a hook that runs `messagesTransformHook` first (so TTSR sees all assistants for rule scanning) then `prefillGuardHook` (so anything TTSR didn't fix gets stripped).

### Reference pattern

Composition mirrors the existing `messagesTransformHook` wiring at `index.mjs:204`. The guard module follows the same shape as `ttsr.mjs` (factory + closure pattern with `qualityLog` injection).

## Safety

- Session DB is never modified — stripped messages still display in transcript history.
- Tool-call flows are preserved (only assistants with no live tool calls are stripped).
- Never throws — try/catch with diagnostic logging.
- Composition order: TTSR runs first (it scans the last 3 assistants for rule violations and may append a synthetic user correction); guard runs second so if TTSR didn't append a correction AND the conversation still ends with an assistant, we strip it.

## Verification

1. `node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/prefill-guard.mjs` (syntax)
2. `node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` (syntax)
3. Restart `opencode-web.service` and confirm clean plugin load in `journalctl --user -u opencode-web.service`
4. Send a message via mobile webui that previously triggered the prefill error — should now succeed. Stripped messages produce a journal line: `[aidevops prefill-guard] stripped N trailing assistant message(s) ...`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mobile webui no longer returns prefill error on Claude Opus/Sonnet 4.x
- [ ] Tool-call flows on Claude 4.x continue working (not over-stripped)
- [ ] Plugin loads without errors after restart
- [ ] Journal shows guard activity when stripping occurs
- [ ] No regression in other providers (the guard only strips, never adds)

## Related upstream

- sst/opencode#13768 — original bug report
- sst/opencode#17982 — continuation loop analysis
- sst/opencode#14772 — fix PR (not merged)
- sst/opencode#16921 — alternate fix PR (not merged)
- sst/opencode#18091 — bundled fix PR (not merged)

---

title: Headless worker canary fails across all repos, blocking every pulse dispatch
body:
# Pending issue to post to marcusquinn/aidevops

Drafted 2026-04-07 in opencode interactive session.
GitHub API was rate-limited when we tried to post it; save this file and run the command below when the limit clears.

## Post command

```bash
REPO="marcusquinn/aidevops"
FOOTER=$(~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh footer --model anthropic/claude-opus-4-6)
# Strip this header block before posting; use only the "# Issue body" content below
sed -n '/^# Issue body/,$p' ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/aidevops/canary-failure-issue.md \
  | tail -n +2 \
  | (cat; printf '\n\n%s\n' "$FOOTER") \
  | gh issue create --repo "$REPO" \
      --title "Headless worker canary fails across all repos, blocking every pulse dispatch" \
      --body-file -
```

# Issue body

## Summary

Every headless worker dispatch is failing across all pulse-managed repos with the same error: the pre-dispatch canary test fails (exit 1) within 20 seconds, causing the dispatcher to abort before posting a claim comment. The pulse keeps re-attempting every 2 minutes but no actual work gets done. This is a framework-level regression; project briefs, labels, and dispatch selection are all working correctly.

Also raising a related user preference: **never use Haiku**. The `tier:simple` → haiku mapping should be configurable per-user, and this user wants it changed to Sonnet (or a dedicated "never-haiku" policy). Today it's silently falling through to Sonnet anyway, but the mapping is fragile and needs to be explicit.

## Diagnostic — canary failure

Worker stderr is redirected to `/tmp/pulse-<safe_slug>-<issue>.log` by `dispatch_with_dedup()` in `pulse-wrapper.sh` around line 6983. Every recent log file for every repo shows the identical pattern:

```
[WARNING] Canary test FAILED (exit=1, opencode=1.3.16, timeout=20s)
[WARNING] Output: [aidevops] OAuth pool: detected Claude CLI v2.1.92, OpenCode v1.3.16
[aidevops] Observability: SQLite DB ready at ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/observability/llm-requests.db
[aidevops] OAuth pool: seeded auth entry for anthropic-pool
[aidevops] OAuth pool: seeded auth entry for openai-pool
[aidevops] OAuth pool: seeded auth entry for cursor-pool
[WARNING] Canary failed — aborting dispatch for session issue-N (no claim posted)
```

Notable observations:

1. **OpenCode is launching successfully** — the "OAuth pool: detected" and "SQLite DB ready" lines are from aidevops' own startup hooks running INSIDE OpenCode's sandbox, so we know OpenCode v1.3.16 at least boots far enough to run the hook.
2. **Canary probe fails silently** — exit 1 with no captured error message beyond the seeded-auth lines. Whatever the canary actually tests (prompt? auth check? model selection?) is failing without producing diagnostic output.
3. **Timeout is 20s** — so this is not a "canary took too long" case, it's a genuine exit-1 failure.
4. **Cross-repo impact** — same failure in `/tmp/pulse-Ultimate-Multisite-cli-abilities-bridge-*`, `/tmp/pulse-Ultimate-Multisite-tutor-multisite-compatibilty-*`, and many others. **Not specific to any one repo.**
5. **Dispatch ledger records status "failed"** with the model `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` recorded, meaning model selection succeeded — the failure is downstream of selection.

## Environment at time of failure

### OAuth pool status

```
anthropic pool:
  Total accounts : 1
  Available now  : 1
  Active/idle    : 1
  Rate limited   : 0
  Auth errors    : 0
Pool file: /home/dave/.aidevops/oauth-pool.json

Accounts:
  1. dave@codesolutions.expert [active]
```

Pool reports healthy, but "active" is a cached flag and may not reflect live token validity.

### Headless runtime backoff state

```
headless-runtime-helper.sh backoff status:
  pulse/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 | rate_limit | 2026-04-06T05:13:52Z | 2026-04-06T05:12:54Z
```

**Stale row from 2026-04-06** (two days old). The `retry_after` field is long expired, so it shouldn't block selection — and indeed `headless-runtime-helper.sh select --role worker` correctly returns `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`. But the row is still there, which suggests `backoff clear` never got called for this model after the rate-limit window expired. Possibly unrelated to the canary failure but worth cleaning up.

### Model resolution

```
$ headless-runtime-helper.sh select --role worker
anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
$ echo "exit=$?"
exit=0
```

Selection works. The failure is between selection and actual worker launch — i.e., inside whatever runs the canary probe.

### GitHub API rate limit (secondary symptom)

The pulse is hitting `GraphQL: API rate limit already exceeded for user ID 1534605` on prefetch calls for multiple repos. This appears to be a separate consequence of the pulse retrying failed dispatches every 2 minutes for hours — each retry fetches issue metadata, and eventually hits the per-hour secondary limit. **Stopping the bleeding on individual issues (by labeling them `status:blocked`) reduces pulse churn but doesn't solve the root cause.**

**This tracking issue itself could not be created interactively because of the same rate limit.** The body was drafted in-session and stashed at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/aidevops/canary-failure-issue.md` for posting once the limit clears.

### Relevant versions

- OpenCode: `1.3.16` (as reported by the canary failure output)
- Claude CLI: `v2.1.92` (detected by the OAuth pool startup)
- aidevops framework: whatever `aidevops --version` returns on the affected machine

## Reproduction

On any machine where the pulse is currently failing:

1. `gh issue create` on any pulse-enabled repo with no blocking labels.
2. Wait up to 2 minutes for the pulse timer (`aidevops-supervisor-pulse.timer`) to fire.
3. `tail -f /tmp/pulse-*.log` while it runs.
4. Observe the canary failure pattern shown above.
5. Confirm with `tail ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/dispatch-ledger.jsonl` that the dispatch is recorded with `status: "failed"`.

## Suggested investigation path

1. **Find the canary implementation.** It's called from `dispatch_with_dedup()` or a helper it calls in `pulse-wrapper.sh`. Probably lives in `headless-runtime-helper.sh` or a sibling like `canary-helper.sh` / `worker-launch-helper.sh`. `rg -n "Canary test|canary_test|run_canary" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`.
2. **Run the canary manually and capture stderr.** Reproduce the exact command the dispatcher runs (same env, same model, same `opencode run` flags), but with `2>&1` unredirected, and see what the real failure is.
3. **Candidates to investigate:**
   - OAuth token expired but cached state still says "active" (force a refresh: `oauth-pool-helper.sh refresh anthropic`)
   - OpenCode 1.3.16 regression in how it handles the canary prompt (downgrade test? upstream issue?)
   - Canary prompt itself hitting a provider endpoint that's genuinely rate-limited (not the stale backoff row — the live endpoint)
   - Recent framework update to canary probe broke its own exit handling (`git log` on `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` for the last few days)
4. **Quick wins to try regardless:**
   - `headless-runtime-helper.sh backoff clear anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` to drop the stale row
   - `oauth-pool-helper.sh refresh anthropic` to force token refresh
   - Restart the timer: `systemctl --user restart aidevops-supervisor-pulse.timer`

## Related user preference: never use Haiku (separate fix)

User prefers to never dispatch workers on Haiku models. Today:

- `tier:simple` label is supposed to map to Haiku per `reference/task-taxonomy.md`
- Dispatch ledger shows `tier:simple` tasks actually resolving to `claude-sonnet-4-6` in practice (unclear whether this is intentional round-robin override or a broken tier mapping)
- Either way, the user wants an explicit "never Haiku" policy that can't be circumvented by round-robin

**Proposed solution (sketch):**

Add a user-level config option in `~/.config/aidevops/` (e.g. `runtime.json`) with a `"excluded_models"` or `"tier_overrides"` key:

```json
{
  "tier_overrides": {
    "simple": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"
  },
  "excluded_models": ["anthropic/claude-haiku-*"]
}
```

The `headless-runtime-helper.sh select` function should read this config and apply exclusions before returning a model. The tier override takes precedence over the taxonomy default. This keeps the framework defaults intact while letting individual users express hard preferences.

**Minimal interim fix** (if the config layer is too much work right now): just map `tier:simple` to Sonnet in the framework default, since that's what's already happening in practice. Document as "Haiku is no longer the default for tier:simple because of reliability concerns" in the taxonomy reference.

## Workarounds currently in place

1. Issues `#5` and `#6` on `Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-ai-connector-webllm` have been manually labelled `status:blocked` with an explanatory comment to stop the pulse from hammering them every 2 minutes. They're ready to be unblocked once the canary is fixed.
2. No other action taken. All other pulse-enabled repos are still receiving the canary failures — they'll need bulk mitigation or should just wait for the fix.

## Scope of impact

- **Affected:** all pulse-enabled repos with dispatchable issues (~40 in `PULSE_SCOPE_REPOS`)
- **Duration:** unknown — at minimum since this session started (several hours), possibly longer
- **Severity:** high. The pulse is functionally unable to dispatch any worker. Manual interactive sessions still work (this investigation happened in one).
- **User impact:** the "backlog clears itself overnight" value of the pulse is silently not working. Every dispatch attempt posts a claim comment that gets abandoned. Over hours, that's a lot of noise on issues.

title: fix(upgrade-planning): extracts template placeholders (tXXX/tYYY/tZZZ) from Format section as real tasks
body:
## What

`aidevops upgrade-planning` extracts **template example lines** from the `## Format` section of `TODO.md` and inserts them into `## Backlog` as if they were real tasks.

After running the upgrade (v1.0 → v1.1), the Backlog contained:

```markdown
- [ ] tXXX Task description @owner #tag ~4h (ai:2h test:1h read:30m) logged:2025-01-15
- [ ] tYYY Dependent task blocked-by:tXXX ~2h
- [ ] tXXX.1 Subtask of tXXX ~1h
- [x] tZZZ Completed task ~2h actual:1.5h logged:2025-01-10 completed:2025-01-15
```

These are **format documentation examples**, not actual tasks. The ID placeholders `tXXX`, `tYYY`, `tZZZ` should never appear as real task IDs.

## Why

Any project using `aidevops upgrade-planning` will end up with polluted Backlog sections containing bogus `tXXX`-ID tasks. These then appear to the pulse dispatcher, issue-sync, and human reviewers as real pending work. Breaks trust in the tool.

Reproduced in <webapp> on 2026-04-08 against `aidevops` v3.6.161 / v3.6.165. The upgrade was immediately reverted and a new develop worktree was cleaned up.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd /path/to/any-project-with-TODO.md  # v1.0 format
yes "y" | aidevops upgrade-planning
rg -n '^- \[[ x-]\] (tXXX|tYYY|tZZZ|tXXX\.1)' TODO.md
# Expect: 4 lines found
```

## Root cause

The task extraction parser reads ALL lines matching `^- \[[ x-]\] tNNN ...` across the entire file, including inside the `## Format` section where the template examples live. It should either:

- Skip the `## Format` section entirely
- Or reject task IDs that don't match the real pattern (e.g., reject `t[^0-9]` or non-numeric suffix)

## How

Find the upgrade-planning script:

```bash
rg -n "upgrade-planning|extractTasks|backlog" ~/Git/aidevops/setup-modules ~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts
```

Likely location: `~/Git/aidevops/setup-modules/upgrade-planning.sh` or similar. Fix options:

1. **Section-aware parser:** track current `## Section` header during parse; skip lines when inside `## Format`
2. **ID validator:** filter out task IDs that don't match `^t[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*$` (numeric only)

Option 2 is smaller and more defensive — rejects ALL malformed IDs, not just the specific placeholders. Apply both for belt-and-braces.

Also fix the template itself: `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/templates/todo-template.md` — consider moving the format examples into an HTML comment block `<!-- ... -->` so they're invisible to any parser.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Running `aidevops upgrade-planning` on a v1.0 TODO.md no longer produces `tXXX`/`tYYY`/`tZZZ` lines in the output
- [ ] Real tasks (with numeric IDs) are still preserved through the upgrade
- [ ] Regression test added that runs upgrade-planning on a fixture file and asserts no placeholder IDs in output
- [ ] Fix is in the published v3.6.16x+1 release

## Verification

```bash
# In a temp project with v1.0 TODO.md fixture:
yes "y" | aidevops upgrade-planning
rg -n '^- \[[ x-]\] (tXXX|tYYY|tZZZ)' TODO.md
# Expect: empty
```

title: fix(upgrade-planning): loses ### subsection headers in Backlog — semantic data loss
body:
## What

`aidevops upgrade-planning` **destroys `### Subsection` headers** inside `## Backlog`, flattening all tasks into a single un-grouped list.

Before upgrade (v1.0 TODO.md in <webapp>):

```markdown
## Backlog

### Personal AI Agent Pivot (p006)

- [ ] t200 ...
- [ ] t201 ...

### Framework Testing (March 2026)

- [ ] t...

### p005: Entity Manager

- [ ] t...

### @donna's Methodology Gap Analysis (March 2026)

- [ ] t...

### Launch Readiness

- [ ] t...
```

After upgrade (v1.1):

```markdown
## Backlog

<!--TOON:backlog[0]{id,desc,owner,tags,est,risk,logged,status}:-->

- [ ] t200 ... (everything flat, grouping lost)
- [ ] t201 ...
- [ ] ...
```

## Why

The sub-section headers are **semantic organization** — the user deliberately groups tasks by project/initiative/theme. The upgrade silently discards this structure, treating `###` headers as decoration. This is **semantic data loss** that can't be automatically recovered; the user has to remember the groupings and re-apply them manually.

For any project with many tasks, this turns a navigable Backlog into an indistinguishable pile.

Reproduced in <webapp> on 2026-04-08 against `aidevops` v3.6.161. Upgrade was reverted.

## Reproduction

See sibling issue `FW1` for the bash reproduction. Compare `TODO.md.bak` and `TODO.md` after upgrade — the `###` headers are gone.

## Root cause

The task extraction parser in `upgrade-planning` reads tasks into a flat list and rewrites them under the top-level `##` headers only. There's no model for nested `###` sub-sections.

## How

Options (pick one or combine):

1. **Preserve `###` headers verbatim** during parse/rewrite. Track current `###` per task and re-emit the header before the first task under it when writing the new file.
2. **Encode sub-section as a task tag.** E.g., auto-add `#subsection:p006` or `#group:Launch Readiness` to each task, and use those tags for grouping in future views. Loses the `###` headers but preserves the semantic info in a machine-readable form.
3. **Skip Backlog reorganization entirely** — upgrade only the header metadata and TOON annotations, leave the existing task list bodies (including `###` headers) untouched.

**Recommended: Option 3** is the safest — do the absolute minimum in upgrade-planning. Just:

- Add the TOON header comment (`<!--TOON:backlog[0]:...-->`)
- Add the `risk:` field hint to the format docs
- Bump the format version marker
- Don't touch existing task lines or section headers at all

This minimal approach avoids the risk of ANY data loss during upgrade.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Running `aidevops upgrade-planning` on a v1.0 TODO.md preserves all `### Subsection` headers
- [ ] Task ordering within each subsection is preserved
- [ ] Regression test: fixture with subsections, assert subsections are present in output
- [ ] Fix released in v3.6.16x+1

title: fix(schedulers): aidevops update exits 1 due to unbound variable in schedulers.sh line 613
body:
## What

`aidevops update` exits with code **1** at the end of an otherwise-successful update due to an unbound variable in `schedulers.sh`:

```
[INFO] Supervisor pulse enabled (every 2 min) (systemd user timer)
[schedulers] Removed pre-existing cron entry for aidevops: supervisor-pulse (migrated to systemd)
/home/alexey/Git/aidevops/setup-modules/schedulers.sh: line 613: 12: unbound variable
[WARN] Setup exited with code 1
[OK] Updated to version 3.6.161 (agents deployed)
```

The update itself **succeeds** — framework version is bumped, agents are deployed, MCPs are configured — but the non-zero exit code can break CI pipelines, automation scripts, and anyone who checks `$?` after the update.

## Why

- **CI/automation breakage:** any wrapper that does `aidevops update && run-something` silently skips `run-something`
- **User confusion:** "did the update succeed or not?" — the `[OK] Updated to version 3.6.161` suggests yes, but exit 1 suggests no
- **Observed:** this session's auto-update polling triggered the same behaviour at least twice; framework appears to have continued working

## Evidence

From <webapp> QA session 2026-04-08, during `aidevops update`:

```
/home/alexey/Git/aidevops/setup-modules/schedulers.sh: line 613: 12: unbound variable
[1;33m[WARN][0m Setup exited with code 1
[0;32m[OK][0m Updated to version 3.6.161 (agents deployed)
```

## Root cause

Script runs under `set -u` (unbound variable detection enabled). At line 613 of `setup-modules/schedulers.sh`, a variable named `12` is referenced — which looks like a positional parameter `$12` that's not set, or a typo where an index was meant as a variable name. Without seeing the code, the most likely candidates:

- `$12` referenced without `${12:-}` default
- Array element `${arr[12]}` where index is out of bounds
- Integer `12` being treated as a variable name (shell substitution typo)

## How

1. Open `~/Git/aidevops/setup-modules/schedulers.sh` and navigate to line 613
2. Fix the unbound reference:
   - Add `${VAR:-default}` if it's legit positional param
   - Check bounds before array access
   - Fix typo if it's a variable-name bug
3. Test: `bash -n setup-modules/schedulers.sh` (syntax check) and run the full update path in a test environment
4. Add a regression guard: run `bash -u setup-modules/schedulers.sh --test-mode` in CI

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `aidevops update` exits 0 on a successful update (no unbound variable errors)
- [ ] All existing functionality (cron/systemd migration, pulse enable/disable) still works
- [ ] CI smoke test runs `aidevops update` in a fresh environment and asserts exit 0

## Verification

```bash
aidevops update; echo "exit=$?"
# Expect: exit=0
```

## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/scripts/commands/init-routines.md`
**Detected topic:** Unknown
**Current size:** 73 lines

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)
- Qlty smells resolved for the target file: `~/.qlty/bin/qlty smells --all 2>&1 | grep '.agents/scripts/commands/init-routines.md' | grep -c . | grep -q '^0$'` (report `SKIP` if Qlty is unavailable, not `FAIL`)
- For reference corpora: `wc -l` total of chapter files >= original line count minus index overhead

### Confidence: medium

Automated scan flagged this file for maintainer review. The best simplification strategy requires human judgment — some files are appropriately structured already. Reference corpora (SKILL.md, domain knowledge bases) need restructuring into chapters, not content reduction.

```bash
cmd_name="${cmd_path##*/}"
[[ -z "$cmd_name" ]] && cmd_name="unknown"
```

2. **Batch `_get_process_age`** — instead of calling `ps -p "$pid" -o etime=` per matched process (line 289), collect all matched PIDs in the loop, then make ONE call after the loop:

```bash
# After the pattern-matching loop, batch-fetch etime for all matched PIDs:
local pid_list
pid_list=$(printf '%s,' "${matched_pids[@]}")
pid_list="${pid_list%,}"  # trim trailing comma

# Single ps call for all PIDs
local -A pid_etime_map
while IFS= read -r line; do
    local p_pid p_etime
    p_pid=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $1}')
    p_etime=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $2}')
    pid_etime_map["$p_pid"]="$p_etime"
done < <(ps -p "$pid_list" -o pid=,etime= 2>/dev/null)
```

3. **Bump default interval** (line 94):

```bash
DAEMON_INTERVAL="${MEMORY_DAEMON_INTERVAL:-120}"
```

```bash
[[ -z "$cmd_name" ]] && cmd_name="unknown"
```

2. **Batch `_get_process_age`** — instead of calling `ps -p "$pid" -o etime=` per matched process (line 289), collect all matched PIDs in the loop, then make ONE call after the loop:

```bash
# After the pattern-matching loop, batch-fetch etime for all matched PIDs:
local pid_list
pid_list=$(printf '%s,' "${matched_pids[@]}")
pid_list="${pid_list%,}"  # trim trailing comma

# Single ps call for all PIDs
local -A pid_etime_map
while IFS= read -r line; do
    local p_pid p_etime
    p_pid=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $1}')
    p_etime=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $2}')
    pid_etime_map["$p_pid"]="$p_etime"
done < <(ps -p "$pid_list" -o pid=,etime= 2>/dev/null)
```

title: bug: opencode-aidevops plugin missing @bufbuild/protobuf + headless-runtime-helper does not attach to running opencode server
body:
## Description

Two related bugs in the framework cause `opencode run` to fail with `Error: Session not found`, blocking ALL headless worker dispatch on machines where an `opencode serve` process is running. Both bugs were diagnosed during a 60-minute pulse session that was unable to launch any workers until the deployed scripts were manually patched.

This is distinct from #16978 (closed Apr 4 in v3.6.20). That issue handled "Session not found" caused by stale persisted session IDs. The bugs reported here trigger even when no `--session` flag is passed and no persisted session exists.

---

### Bug 1: opencode-aidevops plugin missing @bufbuild/protobuf dependency

`~/.aidevops/agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/cursor/models.js` imports `@bufbuild/protobuf`:

```js
import { create, fromBinary, toBinary } from "@bufbuild/protobuf";
```

But the plugin's `package.json` has no `dependencies` section, so the module is not installed. Loading the plugin fails:

```
ERROR service=plugin error={"name":"ResolveMessage","message":"Cannot find module '@bufbuild/protobuf' from '/home/dave/.aidevops/agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/cursor/models.js'"} plugin config hook failed
```

This causes the embedded opencode server inside `opencode run` to fail to start, surfacing as `Error: Session not found`.

**Fix:** Add `@bufbuild/protobuf` to the plugin's `package.json` dependencies and have `setup.sh` run `npm install` in the plugin directory after `aidevops update`.

---

### Bug 2: headless-runtime-helper.sh does not attach to running opencode server

When the user has `opencode serve` running on port 4096 (e.g., for the TUI or web client), the environment has `OPENCODE_PID` and `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` set. In this state:

- `opencode run "..." -m anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 --dir /tmp` → fails with `Error: Session not found`
- `opencode run "..." -m anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 --dir /tmp --attach http://localhost:4096 --password "$OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD"` → succeeds

The canary test in `headless-runtime-helper.sh` (`_run_canary_test`, ~line 2548) and the worker dispatch command builder (`_build_run_cmd`, ~line 1349) do not detect `OPENCODE_PID` and do not pass `--attach`/`--password`. Every canary fails, blocking dispatch entirely.

**Fix:** When `OPENCODE_PID` and `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` are set, append `--attach http://localhost:4096 --password "$OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD"` to both the canary and the worker `opencode run` invocation. Verified locally:

```bash
# _build_run_cmd patch (line ~1359)
if [[ -n "${OPENCODE_PID:-}" && -n "${OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD:-}" ]]; then
    printf '%s\0' --attach "http://localhost:4096" --password "${OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD}"
fi

# _run_canary_test patch (line ~2558)
local -a canary_attach_args=()
if [[ -n "${OPENCODE_PID:-}" && -n "${OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD:-}" ]]; then
    canary_attach_args=(--attach "http://localhost:4096" --password "${OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD}")
fi
perl -e "alarm $CANARY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS; exec @ARGV" -- \
    "$OPENCODE_BIN_DEFAULT" run "Reply with exactly: CANARY_OK" \
    -m "$canary_model" --dir "${HOME}" \
    "${canary_attach_args[@]+"${canary_attach_args[@]}"}" \
    >"$canary_output" 2>&1 || canary_exit=$?
```

Both workers dispatched successfully after the patch. Note: port `4096` is the opencode default — a more robust fix would discover the actual port from the running process.

---

## Expected Behavior

1. `opencode-aidevops` plugin loads cleanly without missing-module errors after `aidevops update`.
2. `headless-runtime-helper.sh run` succeeds when called from a session with `OPENCODE_PID` set, without manual patching.
3. The pulse can dispatch workers regardless of whether the user is also running `opencode serve` for interactive use.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have `opencode serve` running on port 4096 (any opencode TUI/web session does this — `OPENCODE_PID` and `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` will be set in the environment).
2. Trigger any pulse cycle or run the canary manually:
   ```bash
   opencode run "Reply with exactly: CANARY_OK" -m anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 --dir "$HOME"
   ```
3. Observe: `Error: Session not found` — no worker spawns.
4. Run with `--attach http://localhost:4096 --password "$OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD"` → succeeds.

Worker logs show:
```
[aidevops] OAuth pool: ...
Error: Session not found
[INFO] [fast-fail] count=1 backoff=600s reason=local_error
```

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.6.167
- **Latest version**: 3.6.170
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.45.0
- **OpenCode version**: 1.3.16 (pinned)
- **OpenCode serve**: running on `0.0.0.0:4096`

## Additional Context

- During the pulse session, four failed worker PIDs (2604559, 2629009, 3372716, 3703540) accumulated before the root cause was diagnosed. Each posted a `DISPATCH_CLAIM` comment and died without spawning, leaving stale claims that blocked re-dispatch for ~30 min via the dispatch-comment TTL.
- After patching both functions, workers for issues #5 and #6 in `Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-ai-connector-webllm` dispatched successfully. Issue #5 was fully completed (PR #14 merged) in the same pulse session.
- The deployed-copy patch will be overwritten by the next `aidevops update`, so this fix needs to land upstream.
- The previous "Session not found" fix in v3.6.20 (#16978) added stale-session detection on retry, but does not handle this case because the canary fails before any retry logic runs.

## Worker Guidance

**Files to modify:**
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` — `_build_run_cmd` (~line 1349) and `_run_canary_test` (~line 2548). When `OPENCODE_PID` and `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` are set, append `--attach <url> --password <password>` to the opencode command. Discover the URL from the running process if possible (e.g., parse `ss -tlnp | grep opencode`), otherwise fall back to `http://localhost:4096`.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/package.json` — add `@bufbuild/protobuf` to `dependencies`.
- `EDIT: setup.sh` (or the relevant plugin install step) — ensure `npm install` runs in the plugin directory after `aidevops update`.

**Reference pattern:** Model the `OPENCODE_PID` guard on the existing `OPENCODE_PID` passthrough at `headless-runtime-helper.sh:151-154` (the env-passthrough block that already knows about this variable).

**Verification:**
```bash
# Bug 1
ls ~/.aidevops/agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/node_modules/@bufbuild/protobuf

# Bug 2 (with opencode serve running)
opencode run "Reply with exactly: CANARY_OK" -m anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 --dir "$HOME"
# Must succeed without --attach flag after fix

# End-to-end
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
ps aux | grep -i opencode | grep -v "serve\|watchdog"  # should show worker processes
```

title: Optimize pulse-session-helper.sh: replace ps loop with single awk pass
body:
## Problem

`pulse-session-helper.sh` parses `ps` output in a loop at line 652:

```bash
ps axo pid,etime,command | grep '[/]full-loop' | grep '\.opencode' | while IFS= read -r line; do
```

This spawns 2 grep processes and reads line-by-line in bash.

## Solution

Replace with single awk pass:

```bash
ps axo pid,etime,command 2>/dev/null | awk '/\/full-loop/ && /\.opencode/ {
    pid=$1; etime=$2
    # Extract title from command
    match($0, /--title[ =]\"([^\"]+)\"/, m)
    title = m[1] ? m[1] : \"untitled\"
    print pid, etime, title
}'
```

## Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-session-helper.sh:652-663` — replace grep|grep|while loop
